_comment: Hierarchical MILP AllGather on rail_optimized_256gpu_dual_plane with switch copy. 256-GPU rail-optimized dual-plane fabric. Every GPU has a port into both planes, so every host transit is co-located (forward dwell 1). Hierarchical only. milp_chunking=4: one MILP chunk = 4 of a host's 8 identities for one destination-cell set, so 2 chunks per host -- between 'holder' (8, intractable here) and 'cell' (1, voids multipath across the 8 uplinks). Bundles span holder GPUs, so three GPUs of each group of four stage through the NVSwitch. switch_copy [true, false]: the network switches of the coarse level copy -- a fan-out is one Send, charged once on its uplink, and ncclize emits it as ONE multicast send threadblock (tb send="r1,r2") with one mscclflowid, plus a switch-JSON (format 2) entry listing every out port; the cell NVSwitches do not copy (multicast there needs NVLS). Pass --no-multicast to ncclize for the pre-multicast output (one unicast send per branch). SLOWEST_LINK keeps every coarse link at >= 1 chunk/epoch (occupancy 1: no multi-epoch legs). objective_type 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) puts makespan first; PAPER (3) ties on it. Outputs: Schedules/<prefix>_flat.json (+ _coarse/_identities/_intra side outputs). EXPERIMENT (branch milp-no-latency-tier): the b4_nows_nodrop input with the MILP latency tier removed, so the tiers are makespan > host_relay > switch_chain (see AllGatherFormulation.hierarchical_objective_tiers). Question: does dropping latency cost flat finish time? Compare against b4_nows_nodrop (2026-11-23: latency -9152, switch_chain 133, flat finish 0.33944, 4565 s). Expect the leaf broadcast: switch_chain 64 (= the root LP bound, so the tier closes at the root once a 64 schedule is found), 248 arrivals in every epoch instead of 256 x 7 + 192, 7-8 last-epoch arrivals per cell instead of 6, summed completion -8928 instead of -9152. What to compare: Schedules/<prefix>_flat.json 4-Collective_Finish_Time against 0.33944, switch_chain, and solve time. No objective_tier_time_limit: the switch_chain tier should close at its root, and with a limit its search would run 90% of it even after reaching 64 (its BestObjStop is the floor 0, not the root bound). time_limit 2 h caps the run if it does not. num_epochs 8 IS the ingress bound (62 chunks into 8 in-links of 1 chunk/epoch), so no horizon past it can help; the leaf broadcast (2 columns per cell over 8 leaves) also takes 8, and the 2026-11-10 dual-plane b4_nows run (solved at 19) finished in exactly 8. symmetry false: no twin-switch flow-equality rows and no switch 'inflow == max(outs)' rule. Both restrict the model (neither is exact for a MILP), and the second costs a gp.max_ per copying-switch row. chunk_symmetry_breaking (default on) orders a host's interchangeable chunks instead, which is exact. See teccl/hierarchy/milp_design.md and teccl/ncclize/multicast_output_design.md.
